taskUsd.description: at most this many dollars per task

capability.description: A capability set: what its holder may do.

channels.description: the channels whose messages act with it

key.description: an API key that holds it, as `${secret:NAME}`

agents.description: the agent profiles that get it (empty: every one)

crew.description: A crew member: who they are, what runs their jobs, when they check in.

brief.description: the standing instructions every job of theirs starts with

kit.description: their kit: `[{ name, description?, body }]` skills and notes

sandbox.description: '' | job | own: a worktree per job, or one of their own

team.description: who they delegate to: `[{ crew, why? }]`

what else wakes them (ADR-0043): triggers whose target is this member (`on: crew.reported`,

crew.title: CrewSpec

perRun.description: USD a run (the run is stopped past it, by wisp.budget's guard)

crew.description: a crew member gets the work instead (a wake)

followUp.description: or a follow-up to the task the event came from

`X-PagerDuty-Signature`): an HMAC-SHA256 of the body under the secret, hex, with or without `sha256=`/`v1=`.

match.description: any other field of the source, matched against the event's payload (a string, a glob, or a list)

project.description: the project it watches, and the folder its task runs in

prompt.description: or a prompt of its own: `{event.summary}`, `{event.payload.x}` are filled in

task.description: the declared task it starts (its `{params}` from the event)

tz.description: schedule and `when`: an IANA zone ("Europe/Zurich"); this computer's by default

users.description: chat.message: who may (names or ids; `anyone` for an open channel)

workflow.description: or a workflow runs, with the event as its input

crew.When.description: When a trigger may run: outside these, an event is skipped or queued until the window opens.

days.description: mon tue wed thu fri sat sun (every day when empty)

maxRounds.description: turns a goal may take before it stops and asks

text.description: what has to be true for it to be met ("npm test passes and the build is green")

harness.description: A harness CLI: where it comes from, which version is trusted, its own defaults.

enabled.description: installed or not (false: wisp never offers it)

lean.description: lean runs: wisp's short base prompt instead of the harness's own

liveLimits.description: read its usage limits while it runs

pin.description: the version wisp trusts (a newer one asks first); `from: npm` installs this one

harness.title: HarnessSpec

machine.description: A computer: this one (`this`) or a peer wisp reaches.

address.description: its address (host, ssh target or grid name)

onGrid.description: this computer is on the grid, so other computers reach it

port.description: its wisp's port (ssh, loopback), when it isn't the default

machine.MachineLimits.description: What a computer may take on before automations wait.

cpuCeiling.description: automations wait while the CPU stays over this percent of its cores

heavyLock.description: one heavy step (a build, the tests) at a time

maxRuns.description: runs at once (default: one per 3 GB of memory)

memoryFloor.description: automations wait while free memory is under this percent

notification.description: What notifies where: events to a channel or a webhook (v1 `notify`, `drainWatch`, `webhookTriggers`).

projects.description: only for these projects (empty: every one)

onError.description: on an error: escalate (a stronger model) | retry | stop

review.description: a review by this agent profile after each run

pipeline.title: PipelineSpec

source.description: where a user's plugin comes from: a path, `gist:<id>` or a URL

project.description: A project: a folder wisp works in, and how.

agent.description: the agent profile or harness its tasks use unless they say

path.description: the folder (absolute), or a repo URL cloned into the worktree dir

run.description: commands that start the project (a dev server), for Run

test.description: the command that runs its tests (Auto learns from whether a task's tests pass)

project.title: ProjectSpec

project.ProjectTrust.description: What a project trusts without asking: its hooks, MCP servers and setup script.

mcp.description: the project's own MCP servers, by name

cleanupDays.description: days a finished task's worktree stays before cleanup

enabled.description: each task in a worktree of its own

fixConflicts.description: resolve merge conflicts with an agent

include.description: untracked files copied into each worktree (`.env`, `node_modules`)

max.description: at most this many worktrees at once

onDone.description: when a task is done: ask | remove-clean | keep

accounts.updateCheck.description: Check for newer harness versions: once a day, wisp asks npm for the latest Claude Code, Codex and opencode (npm then knows which of them you have)

automations.webhookTriggers.description: Webhook triggers: other services may start this computer's webhook triggers (POST /api/triggers/<name> with its secret)

budget.drainWatch.description: Drain watch: tell the phone when a plan moves much faster than usual for the same work

budget.limitHold.description: Ask near the limit: before a task would take a usage window past this percent, ask first (automations wait for the reset)

budget.liveLimits.description: Check Codex while work waits: read its usage every 10 minutes while work waits for its plan (spends nothing)

budget.windowNotice.description: Window notices: say when a usage window changed length or resets early

channels.project.description: Default project: where a task from a channel (Slack, Discord, Telegram, email) runs when its message names none ('': the last used)

crew.tint.description: Crew tint: with the crew rail, the task list takes a very light tint of the colour of the member you pick.

git.cloneDir.description: Where a pasted repo URL is cloned ('': the first of ~/code, ~/dev, ~/Developer, ~/projects… that exists, else ~/code)

learn.enabled.description: Learn from your tasks: a short retro after each quiet task, kept as preferences and lessons later tasks follow

machine.batteryHold.description: On battery under this percent, check-ins and the crew queue wait

machine.memoryFloor.description: Automations wait while free memory is under this percent

runtime.apps.description: Interactive answers: agents may answer with a small app

runtime.blocks.description: wisp blocks: answers come as cards (off: plain markdown)

runtime.followUp.description: A follow-up while a task works: interrupt it, or queue after it

runtime.retentionDays.description: Days a finished task stays in the list before it's archived (0: always)

runtime.teams.description: Delegate's saved teams (presets): [{ id, name, members: [{ name, agent, model?, effort?, use?, count?, machine? }] }]; Presets picks one, Save as preset keeps one (v1 config.teams)

runtime.watch.description: Watch agents work: agents may open what they built in wisp's browser to check it

settings.transcript.description: Open tasks on their transcript instead of the answer
